instruction.text: Decide whether the statements are true or false.

atoms.a: The Battle of Waterloo marked the beginning of the Pax Britannica.
Britishness is a clearly defined term.
The BBC is the UK's oldest and largest local and global broadcaster.
Suffrage for all citizens was introduced in 1818.

wrong.text: Suffrage was granted to all men over 21 in 1918, and to women in 1928.

atoms.a: The defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588 marked beginning of Great Britain's emergence as a major naval power.
The NHS is the national broadcasting company.

wrong.text: NHS stands for National Health Service.

atoms.a: During the First World War, Britain was a leading Allied power.
Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales play no part in British identity.
English functions as the UK's dominant language.
British people are perceived as very calm football fans.

wrong.text: They are known for football hooliganism.

atoms.a: National identity may often be in contrast with regional identity.
British weather is said to be very warm and sunny.

wrong.text: According to stereotypes, it rains a lot in the UK.

atoms.a: Despite the lack of a clear definition , ethically uniform stereotypes of Britishness persist.
During and after the Tudor period, no relevant political and religious events took place.

wrong.text: From the Tudor period to 1901, Britain experienced key religious and political changes.

atoms.a: In 1215, the Magna Carta marked the first limitation of royal power by the nobility.
Ireland has never been part of the United Kingdom.

wrong.text: In 1801, Ireland joined the United Kingdom.

atoms.a: The late medieval period was dominated by conflict, culminating in the Wars of the Roses.
The overthrow of James II and establishment of a constitutional monarchy in 1688/89 is known as the Wars of the Roses.

wrong.text: It is called the Glorious Revolution.

atoms.a: Chicken Tikka Masala is a very popular dish in the UK, which originated in India.
William Shakespeare was a renowned Irish poet and playwright.
Terminology
atoms.b: Great ((Britain)) is the term for the largest island in the British Isles. It consists of the countries ((++England ++Scotland)), ((++England ++Scotland)) and Wales. It is a geographical term, whereas the ((United)) Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern ((Ireland)) is a sovereign country and thus a political term.

atoms.a: Britishness and Stereotypes
atoms.b: Britishness is often understood as a synonym for ((++Englishness ++English ++England ++being_English)), even though Scottish, Northern Irish and ((Welsh)) play equally important roles. Some stereotypes may serve nationalistic purposes, but others such as the apparently always ((++bad ++horrible ++rainy)) weather are neutral in terms of ideas about British ethnic identity.

atoms.a: Contrasts in British Identity
atoms.b: British identity has many different and sometimes opposing aspects. For example, modern democracy is contrasted by the historical continuity of the ((monarchy)), with the king or queen still maintaining an important role. As of lately, the act of the UK leaving the EU, called the ((Brexit)), has left the question of European integration unanswered.
